rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Turning away from the message amounts to denying it, so the audience has in fact made denial real.
rows.anchor: ولما كان حال المعرض عن الشيء حال المكذب به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The consequence particle makes the threatened outcome follow from denial; the sīn confirms its arrival while allowing little respite.
rows.anchor: ليعلموا أن ما كذبوا به واقع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mocked reports are the punishment and consequences they denied; denial makes the warning seem trivial and exposes it to ridicule.
rows.anchor: لأن من كذب بشيء خف عنده قدره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse uses ḥadhf al-iḥtibāk: denial in the first clause signals omitted denial in the second, and mockery in the second signals omitted mockery in the first.
rows.anchor: ذكر التكذيب أولا دليلا على حذفه ثانيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The earth’s signs continue the preceding call to reflect on the heavens, including their constellations and associated signs.
rows.anchor: وكان قد تقدم آخر تلك الحث على تدبر بروج السماء وما يتبعها من الدلالات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording turns attention toward the earth’s broad extent, varied regions, and soils; its preposition marks a limit or direction and hints at their failure to reflect.
rows.anchor: عبر للدلالة عليه بحرف الغاية فقال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s abundant growth in the earth follows its being barren and lifeless, displaying divine greatness.
rows.anchor: بعد أن كانت يابسة ميتة لا نبات بها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zawj here means a class or kind whose members resemble one another; God abundantly grew every kind useful to them in this life.
rows.anchor: فلم يبق صنف يليق بهم في العاجلة إلا أكثرنا من الإنبات منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Karīm describes what is valued and praised in its category: abundant in benefits, good in outcome, and free of impurity; the many varied plants are watered by one water.
rows.anchor: على اختلاف ألوانها في زهورها وأنوارها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The extraordinary growth, together with preceding admonitions, is a sufficient sign of the Creator’s power over resurrection and other matters, calling people to faith and restraining transgression.
rows.anchor: منبها له في كل حال على عظيم اقتدار صانعه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The singular sign amid many signs indicates equal evidentiary force: one sign suffices for the firmly grounded, while others heed none.
rows.anchor: فالراسخون تغنيهم واحدة , وغيرهم لا يرجعون لشيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most people did not become deeply rooted believers, as in the statement that most believe in God while associating partners with Him.
rows.anchor: لأنه ( ما يؤمن أكثرهم بالله إلا وهم مشركون )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is able to compel people to faith or punish them, yet mercifully delays punishment and sends the Book to clarify what He approves and establish proof.
rows.anchor: أي القادر على كل من قسرهم على الإيمان

rows.speaker: أبو حيان
rows.claim: Abū Ḥayyān explains the pairing as God’s might in punishing unbelievers and mercy toward the believers of every community.
rows.anchor: قال أبو حيان : والمعنى أنه عز في نقمته من الكفار , ورحم مؤمني كل أمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The narrative exemplifies the preceding ending of al-Furqān: God’s power to seize those ungrateful for blessings and resistant to messengers, while consoling Muhammad through earlier prophetic trials.
rows.anchor: في إظهار القدرة بالبطش عندالنقمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The accounts are presented as true history that nearby People of the Book could not deny, proving that the Qur’an is from the Lord of the worlds, not soothsaying or poetry, despite widespread unbelief.
rows.anchor: فصح قطعا أن هذا الكتاب جلي الأمر , على القدر , ليس بكهانة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s mercy sustains bodies with needed provisions and religions through messengers and books; after long indulgence in heedlessness, punishment discloses His might and consoles the Prophet.
rows.anchor: بما فيه حياة أديانهم بإرسال الرسل وإنزال الكتب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prophetic histories display might, which brings destruction, and mercy, which grants delay; the ordering teaches that punishment follows clear exposition and a lengthy respite.
rows.anchor: فلا يعذب إلا بعد البيان مع طول الإمهال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham’s account omits the destruction of a people, signaling gentleness and delay for Abraham’s Arab descendants, as in the sending of the Qur’an and Muhammad.
rows.anchor: إشارة غلى البشارة بالرفق ببنية العرب في الإمهال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses and Abraham offer the fullest consolation because of their closeness to Muhammad and shared migration and journey toward the Holy Land; Moses is placed first.
rows.anchor: وكانت التسلية بموسى وإبراهيم عليهما السلام أتم , لما لهما من القرب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses especially parallels this community through his unmatched scripture and signs, his people’s guidance and preservation, later prophets and conquests, and Israel’s proximity to the Arabs in Medina.
rows.anchor: بالكتاب الذي ما بعد القرآن مثله والآيات التي ما أتى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because Jews lived nearby and could confirm the account or be asked about it, the story’s public familiarity would make their acknowledgment a powerful proof.
rows.anchor: مع مجاورتهم للعرب حتى في دار الهجرة , وموطن النصرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: As warning, the clause can mean remember God’s long merciful delay for Muhammad’s people.
rows.anchor: اذكر أثر رحمتنا بطول إمهالنا لقومك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the warning reading, the audience is treated as having seen Moses’ call because Jews were nearby: they knew the story or could ask them about it.
rows.anchor: لأن اليهود في بلادهم وفي حد القرب منهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The people meant are Pharaoh’s people, deeply unjust through disbelief, wronging themselves, the Israelites, and other servants.
rows.anchor: وظلم بني إسرائيل وغيرهم من العباد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question is an accusatory appeal for them to become God-fearing; it conveys severe anger, records their injustice, and marvels that long respite has only increased their stubbornness.
rows.anchor: في سياق الإنكار عليهم , والإيذان بشديد الغضب منهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Knowing that people resist what opposes their desires, the account anticipates Moses asking for divine help, in a manner compared with the complaint in 25:30.
rows.anchor: بقوله ملتفتا إلى نحو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The people of Hell lament that they have no sincere friend who truly loves them and could benefit them, since a friend need not be able to intercede.
rows.anchor: قالوا تأسفا على أقل ما يمكن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḥamīm means a close relative; its root sense is a devoted companion pained by what pains the other person.
rows.anchor: أي قريب , وأصله المصافي الذي يحرقه ما يحرقك ,

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The singular indefinite generalizes the negation and suggests that such a friend is intrinsically rare or wholly absent.
rows.anchor: وأفرد تعميما للنفي وإشارة إلى قلته في حد ذاته أو عدمه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After escape becomes impossible, they wish for an impossible return to worldly life so they could become enduring believers and enter Paradise.
rows.anchor: قالوا : { فلو لنا كرة } أي رجعة إلى الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham’s account is a great warning against associating partners with God and a call to faith, through his proof against idols, proof of God’s exclusive right to worship, threats, promises, and guidance to prepare during life’s respite.
rows.anchor: في هذه القصة أعظم زاجرا عن الشرك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Despite witnessing and hearing this powerful proof, most did not become steadfast believers; this consoles Muhammad through the example of his great forefather.
rows.anchor: الذين شهدوا منه هذا الأمر العظيم والذين سمعوه عنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God can punish every opponent, yet mercifully delays sinners, provides blessings, sends messengers, and lays out law; He destroys only after establishing proof.
rows.anchor: في إمهاله العصاة مع إدرار النعم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After Abraham, Noah’s account comes as that of the second father, older in time, showing that trial is ancient and displaying both long respite and eventual universal punishment.
rows.anchor: قصة الأب الثاني , مقدما لها على غيرها , لما له من القدم في الزمان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The feminine verb form is deliberately chosen although masculine agreement with qawm is more common: it marks their deed as vile or their people as insignificant despite their power.
rows.anchor: اختيارا للتأنيث - وأن كان تذكير القوم أشهر -

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Noah’s people means all humanity on earth before peoples divided through the separation of languages.
rows.anchor: وهو أهل الأرض كلهم من الآدميين قبل اختلاف الأمم

rows.speaker: البغوي
rows.claim: Al-Baghawī transmits the explanation that denying Noah amounts to denying all messengers, since one who rejects a single messenger’s miracle rejects what all brought.
rows.anchor: من كذب بمعجزة واحدة فقد كذب الكل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Noah’s people did not pause to request evidence or seek a gracious approach before responding to his call.
rows.anchor: لم يتأنوا بطلب دليل , ولا ابتغاء وجه جميل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling Noah their brother recalls his kinship with them and consoles Muhammad; the expression also models good manners and gentleness in winning them over.
rows.anchor: زيادة في تسلية هذا النبي الكريم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Noah presents himself as sharing his people’s pain and joy, which grounds his concern that they protect themselves from God’s anger through monotheism.
rows.anchor: مع كوني أخاكم يسوءني ما يسوءكم ويسرني ما يسركم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He is a messenger from their Creator and therefore has no option but to convey what he was commanded.
rows.anchor: أي من عند خالقكم , فلا مندوحة لي عند إبلاغ ما أمرت به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: His people’s long familiarity establishes that he is neither deceitful nor treacherous, so he must deliver the entire message.
rows.anchor: أمين * } أي لا غش عندي كما تعلمون ذلك مني على طول خبرتكم بي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After the gentle invitation and proof of his trustworthiness, Noah gives a decisive command: fear God through monotheism for salvation, and obey him in all commands to avoid punishment.
rows.anchor: بما ثبت به أمرها , تسبب عنه الجزم بالأمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Having established his trustworthiness, Noah denies any ulterior motive; min intensifies the denial so no one suspects his call is a means to earn payment.
rows.anchor: ليظن ظان أني جعلت الدعاء سببا له

words: إن أجري إلا على رب العالمين
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He reinforces that his reward for inviting them belongs solely to the Lord of all creatures, who governs and nurtures them.
rows.anchor: أي الذي دبر جميع الخلائق ورباهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Noah repeats the appeal after removing suspicion about payment to show deep concern and emphasize the grave command to a coarse, resistant people.
rows.anchor: فأعاده إعلاما بالاهتمام بذلك زيادة في الشفقة عليهم وتأكيدا له في قلوبهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The elite refuse belief because poor followers would become their equals; they view worldly rank as a reason not to follow Noah, as Quraysh did regarding Muhammad’s companions.
rows.anchor: استنادا إلى داء الكبر الذي ينشأ منه بطر الحق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The poor followers’ undistracted, humbled hearts are more open to goodness; followers of messengers commonly come from the poor, a pattern Heraclius also asked about.
rows.anchor: لأن الله تعالى عند المنكسرة قلوبهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The proud are like someone who would rather remain a rank lower than rise to a level shared with a former inferior, exposing the folly of status pride.
rows.anchor: فكان مثال المستكبرين مثال شخص كان آخر دونه بدرجة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Noah says their earlier conduct is not his concern; he sees their good outward state and does not investigate what preceded their following him.
rows.anchor: وما لي وللبحث عن ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: True nobility comes from religion and piety rather than wealth or lineage, so poor followers of low birth are honored by their faith.
rows.anchor: فإن الغني غني الدين , ولانسب نسب التقوى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Only God, who knows their inward states, accounts for their past and future deeds; awareness of the Last Day would stop the elite’s worldly objection.
rows.anchor: المختص بضبط جميع الأعمال والحساب عليها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Noah will not expel believers whose faith has become firmly rooted, whether to induce the elites’ belief or satisfy their desires.
rows.anchor: صار الإيمان لهم وصفا راسخا فلم يرتدوا عنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Noah is only a clear warner: he is not tasked with probing inward states or imposing demands on followers, and he explains his message without obscurity.
rows.anchor: لا وكيل مناقش على البواطن , ولا متعنت على الأتباع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When Noah rejects their demand to expel the followers, they abandon their deceptive inducement and threaten him with death by stoning.
rows.anchor: ولما أياسهم مما أرادوا من طرد أتباعه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Addressing him by his name instead of a respectful title signals their rudeness and lack of manners.
rows.anchor: ثم سموه باسمه جفاء وقلة أدب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here al-mujrimīn means those to be killed, and Noah’s weak followers will not be able to protect him.
rows.anchor: ولا ينفعك أتباعك هؤلاء الضعفاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After Noah’s rescue aboard the Ark, God drowned those who remained on earth and had not boarded, despite their strength and numbers; this was easy for Him.
rows.anchor: على قوتهم وكثرتهم , وكان ذلك علينا يسيرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The account is a sign to witnesses and hearers that God punishes the disobedient and saves the obedient; no one else controls their guidance or submission.
rows.anchor: عظيمة لمن شاهد ذلك أو سمع به , على أنا ننتقم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most who knew the story still did not believe, though they should have responded to the proof, the first signs of punishment, or the flood itself.
rows.anchor: وقد ينبغي لهم إذ فاتهم الإيمان لمحض الدليل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s might could force obedience or punish at the first sin; His mercy selects devoted servants and sends messengers to explain duties and prohibitions, destroying only after full proof.
rows.anchor: أي القادر بعزته على كل من قسرهم على الطاعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The account turns from Noah to ask whether later peoples learned from the earlier warning; ʿĀd rejected the messengers by turning away from Hud’s miracle.
rows.anchor: المرسلين * } بالإعراض عن معجزة هود عليه الصلاة والسلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hud was their known brother, whose sincerity, counsel, and fidelity they already knew; their failure to pause for reflection emphasizes the immediacy of their rejection.
rows.anchor: وقد عرفوا صدق إخائه , وعظيم نصحه ووفائه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The particle alā introduces a gentle, courteous appeal, softening the exhortation so it might reach them.
rows.anchor: ألا } بصيغة العرض تأدبا معهم وتلطفا بهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hud calls them to fear their Creator by worshipping Him alone and not associating anything powerless to harm or benefit.
rows.anchor: أي تكون منكم تقوى لربكم الذي خلقكم فتعبدوه وحده ولا تشركوا به ما لا يضر ولا ينفع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hud’s commission as messenger is what moves him to call them to fear God.
rows.anchor: إني لكم رسول } أي فهو الذي حملني على أن أقول لكم ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: As a trustworthy messenger, Hud neither conceals any commanded message nor disobeys any part of it.
rows.anchor: أمين } أي لا أكتم عنكم شيئا مما أمرت به ولا أخالف شيئا منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hud concludes that his message requires them to fear God and obey him in all that he commands concerning steadfast reverence.
rows.anchor: الذي هو أعظم من كل شيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hud asks no payment for the call, leaving no grounds to suspect his motive; his reward is only from the Lord of all worlds.
rows.anchor: أجري غلا على رب العالمين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Having called them to faith, Hud censures practices that sustain their misguidance and recalls the ancient flood, which destroyed living creatures and buildings.
rows.anchor: ولما فرغ من الدعاء إلى الأصل , وهو الإيمان بالرسول المرسل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hud first explains rīʿ as a raised place, then criticizes building a monument on every one: if the purpose were guidance, some would suffice.
rows.anchor: بكل ريع } أي مكان مرتفع ؛ قال أبو حيان :

rows.speaker: أبو عبيدة
rows.claim: Abū ʿUbayda gives rīʿ the meaning road.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو عبيدة : الريع الطريق

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujāhid explains rīʿ as the pass between two mountains.
rows.anchor: وقال مجاهد : الفج بين الجبلين

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: An unattributed view takes rīʿ as a path whether traveled or not; the word’s root sense is increase.
rows.anchor: وقيل : السبيل سلك أم لم يسلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A rational person should not waste precious time in pointless play, especially when death lies ahead.
rows.anchor: والعاقل ينبغي له أن يصون أوقاته النفيسة عن العبث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Maṣāniʿ can mean water-holding structures or imposing palaces and fortresses built to endure through the ages.
rows.anchor: مصانع } أي أشياء بأخذ الماء , أو قصورا مشيدة وحصونا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Building such durable works suits people who act as though they expect to live forever; the author says this is the meaning reported from Ibn ʿAbbās.
rows.anchor: فلا يبنيها إلا من حاله حال الراجي للخلود , ولذلك قال : { لعلكم تخلدون

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās, as cited in al-Bukhārī, glosses the phrase as meaning that they act as though they will remain forever.
rows.anchor: في البخاري عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما من تفسيرها بكأنكم
